newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton prices jumped on Thursday mainly on demand from exporters and are likely to remain stable next week, dealers said.

"Cotton demand from exporters has picked up during the last couple of days," dealer Nasim Uslam said. "And the mill owners have also followed the lead, but most of their deals are being done on credit because they are short of funds."
In the kerb market, rates for the NIAB-78 variety were around 2,200 rupees ($54.33) per maund (37.32 k.g.) and for the K-68 around 2,400 rupees, dealers said.
